steps: Check the fireplace & approvals

Masonry fireplace (or Morsø Zero Clearance Enclosure) at least 26" H × 19¼" D × 28¾" W, with a clay or stainless steel liner; remove or lock the damper open. Install to CAN/CSA-B365 with local building approval.

Local building officials have final authority; discuss the installation with them before beginning.

  • Minimum masonry fireplace: 26" / 660 mm high, 19¼" / 490 mm deep, 28¾" / 730 mm wide.
  • Approved: masonry fireplace, or the Morsø Fireplace Insert Zero Clearance Enclosure (separate instructions). Not approved: factory-built fireplace, transportable building / mobile home.
  • Don't move bricks or mortar from the existing fireplace.
  • Confirm clearances and floor protection before you start. The data plate is on the back of the stove.
Remove the door & firebox liners

Pull the split pin on each hinge pin, lift out both hinge pins and take off the door (keep the loose brass washer from the upper hinge). Remove liners in order: bottom, two sides, rear, then the liner and insulation mat above the baffle.

The insert arrives fully assembled; the flue collar can only be removed after the baffle plate comes out.

The liners are very porous and must be handled with great care.
Remove the baffle plate
Four M8 bolts; the plate weighs 30 lbs. Remove the outermost bolt each side, screw in the two guide bolts supplied, remove the two center bolts, then slide the plate off the guide bolts.

1. Remove the outermost bolt on each side.
  2. Screw the two guide bolts into the outermost holes so that the heads are barely visible.
  3. Remove the two center bolts; the plate now rests only on the guide bolts.
  4. Carefully slide the plate off the guide bolts and out of the combustion chamber.
Detach flue collar & combustion chamber

Unscrew the flue collar (with stop bar) and connect it to the flue pipe, 8 feet stainless steel connector or flexible liner in the chimney. Remove the outer trim, loosen the two bolts and pull out the combustion chamber; never lift it by the blower housing door.
Set & level the convection box
Position the convection box in the fireplace opening and level it with the leveling bolts on its base, inside the blower housing. Then refit the combustion chamber.
Connect the liner & reassemble

Guide the flue collar, liner attached, through the circular hole in the back of the convection box and fasten it to the combustion chamber. Refit baffle, liners, insulation mat and door in reverse order.

1. Baffle: hang it on the two guide bolts, fit the two M8 center bolts, remove the guide bolts and fit the last two M8 bolts.
  2. Liners: rear, the two sides, the two bottoms. Lay the insulation mat on the baffle, then fit the last liner in front, centered on the baffle and slanted up toward the smoke exit hole.
  3. Rehang the door on its hinge pins; refit the split pins and the brass washer on the upper hinge.

Where the masonry fireplace was altered for the insert, attach the enclosed metal data tag to the masonry with screws or nails, where it is easily visible. To remove the insert later, reverse the installation steps.
Chimney liner

Continuous 6" liner from the insert to the top of the chimney, one flueway per appliance, sealed airtight and supported independently of the stove. Liner system UL listed to UL 1777 (USA) / ULC S635 (Canada).

Residential masonry or listed type HT factory-built chimney (UL-103-1985 (2100º F.) / ULC S-629). Liner to class 3 of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640. Recommended chimney height at least 16 feet above the stove (not required). Never connect to an air distribution duct or system.

Note: p. 9 says the insert must be installed with a continuous 6" chimney liner from the insert to the top of the chimney; p. 5 says the chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner, with a stainless steel connector at least 8 feet long; and p. 7 says to connect the flue collar to "the flue pipe (or 8 feet stainless steel connector) or the flexible chimney liner".
Chimney connector

Fit the enclosed 6 inch adapter to the flue collar. Connector 6 inches (150mm): 24 MSG black or blue, or listed double-wall, never galvanized; secure with a minimum of three screws to the product and each adjoining section.
Clearances & floor protection

US: 17" sidewall, 26½" mantel and top facing, 8" side facing. Floor protection depends on the height of the door glass above a combustible floor: 21" in front at 6" or more, 16" at 20.25" or more, 8" to each side.
Fit the blower kit

Blower on the base at the rear, centered between the two rectangular vent holes, mouth facing up; thermostat sensor on the heat shield under the firebox. Route the cord out a side cut-out with the cable ties and bolt the speed controller across the front-right grill.

panels.title: Smoke or a sluggish fire
items: Smoke or fumes on lighting or reloading, or a fire that won't respond → poor draft (in a very few cases, too little fresh air into the room)
Stove suddenly sluggish → soot fall around the flue collar or in the flue/chimney
Sluggish or unpredictable performance → connector/chimney significantly larger than 6", flue gases cool too much
Back-puffing and sluggishness → overly dry wood that is gray in color

panels.title: Over-firing & wear
items: Any part of the stove or chimney connector glows → over-firing
Distorted baffle → over-fire; stove still works, efficiency may suffer, replace it
Fast internal wear → persistent heavy firing; soot and ashes left to accumulate

panels.title: Dirty or misting glass
items: Dirty glass → fuel too wet, logs too large or not split, combustion temperatures too low
Soot on the glass → stove run too slowly, or wood not well seasoned
Wood spits or sizzles, glass persistently mists up → wood not properly seasoned

panels.title: Door & reloading
items: Door hard to close, air leaking around it, fire less controllable → hardened rope gasket; replace it
New load won't light → leave the door slightly ajar until the wood kindles
Logs not alight within 2 minutes → in an extreme case the flue gases can ignite; reload only on a good ember layer

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Morsø recommends the top-down method. It's the most environmentally friendly way to light, and it minimizes soot on the glass. A cold stove needs plenty of air at first.

  1. Open the air control fully: slide the handle under the door all the way to the right.
  2. Lay about 4-6 lbs of dry kindling sticks, a layer about 5-6 inches thick. Put two firelighters directly under the top layer of kindling.
  3. Light the fire.
  4. Leave the door open an inch or two. Don't leave the stove unattended while the door is open.
  5. After about 5 minutes, when the chimney is warm, close the door. A good layer of embers forms in about 15-20 minutes. Then reload.
Your very first fire: keep it small so the paint can cure and the stove's main plates can settle into position. The paint gives off some fumes, so ventilate the room.
Note: p. 17 says to use approx. 4-6 lbs of dry kindling; p. 28 says to light with 1 - 2 kg of dry kindling.

If smoke or fumes come out when you light or reload, or the fire won't respond, poor draft is almost certainly the cause. Ask your stove supplier how best to improve the flue's draft.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
You run the fire with one handle: the air control under the door. It slides sideways.

All the way rightFully open · high burn rate
Mid rangeMedium burn rate (recommended)
All the way leftClosed · factory-set minimum low burn rate

This handle sets the primary air, which washes down the inside of the door glass and helps burn off the gases from the fire. The other two air supplies are fixed and can't be changed: secondary air feeds the top of the fire through holes in the tubes under the lower baffle, and pilot air feeds the embers through a hole behind the front grate.

Rules of thumb

  • Less heat: less wood, less air. More heat: more wood, more air. Keep a good layer of embers either way.
  • Before you use the lowest setting, burn at medium for about 15 minutes so the fire is properly established.
  • When you turn the air down, keep enough air for clear, lasting flames.
Don't try to get more heat by altering the air control's range. The minimum low burn rate is set at the factory, and altering it is against federal regulations.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Add wood while there are still glowing embers in the bed. Make sure the ember layer is good first: a new load should light within 2 minutes.

  1. Spread the embers across the bottom, mostly toward the front.
  2. Lay 2-3 pieces across the embers in one or two layers, about 1 inch apart.
  3. Close the door and leave the air control fully open. If the wood doesn't catch, leave the door slightly ajar until it does, then close it.
  4. After a few minutes, set the air control for the heat you want.

Repeat these steps for each new load.

Where the wood goes

  • Keep the load below the back stone and the stainless-steel air baffle box. The space in front of and above the baffle nozzles stays clear for the gases to burn.
  • Keep logs at least one inch from the glass, and never let the fire rest on it.
  • Don't prop the wood up on grates, andirons or anything else.
Note: p. 18 recommends a fuel load of 4 lbs (3 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces); p. 19 recommends 4 lbs (2 pieces) up to 12 lbs (6 pieces), with a maximum of 6 kg/12 lbs (approx. 5-6 split logs) per load; and p. 28 says to refuel with 2 - 3 pieces, no more than 2 - 2.5 kg.

wood.title: What wood to burn
wood.html:
Burn only natural wood that is well seasoned and dry, with no more than 20% moisture. The Morsø Moisture Meter (part # 62929900) checks it easily.

Lengthapprox. 10-11 inches (27 cm)
Thickness, splitapprox. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm)
Weight per piecearound 1.5-2 lbs
Maker's website: Log Size 20".

Seasoning

Split the wood, then stack it under cover in an airy spot where air can move through each piece. Some softwoods season in one good summer; oak, maple and elm can take up to 18 months. Seasoned wood feels light and shows cracks from the center out at the ends. If it spits or sizzles and the glass keeps misting up, it isn't seasoned. Overly dry, gray wood can cause back-puffing and a sluggish fire.

Never burn

  • Driftwood (its salt may cause corrosion) or construction wood that may be treated with chemicals
  • Unseasoned or treated wood, colored paper, cardboard, solvents, trash or garbage
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire. Keep them away from the stove while it's in use.
Note: p. 16 says split wood should be approx. 3 to 3.5 inches (7-8 cm) in section; p. 28 says the fuel must be split and 8 - 12 cm thick.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass & finish
glass.html:
When the stove runs at the right temperatures, there should be little or no dirt on the glass. Dirt from lighting mostly burns off as it heats up.

Heavier deposits

  • Use Morsø glass cleaner on cold glass, following its instructions.
  • Never clean the glass while it's hot, and never use abrasive cleaners.

Why glass gets dirty

  • Wood too wet, or logs too large or not split
  • Fire burning too cool, or the stove run too slowly
Cracked or broken glass: don't use the stove. Replace it right away with Morsø high temperature ceramic glass (part #79560100); don't use substitutes. Avoid striking the glass or slamming the door.

Old ceramic glass can't be recycled with ordinary glass. Hand it in at a recycling station as ceramic glass.

The painted body

The heat-resistant Senotherm paint is best kept clean with a vacuum's soft brush attachment or a lint-free cloth. If it turns slightly gray over time, Morsø touch-up spray paint is available from your stove supplier. Expect a slight smell the first time you fire after touching up, and ventilate the room well.

ash.title: Ash & the off-season
ash.html:
Don't clean out every bit of ash. Once it's established, keep a 1-1.5 inch (2-3 cm) layer of ash on the firebox floor at all times.

Removing ash safely

  • Never empty the stove while it's in operation.
  • Never use a household or shop vacuum to remove ash.
  • Put ashes in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set the closed container on a noncombustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  • If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until all cinders have thoroughly cooled.

Before summer

Clean the stove out thoroughly when the heating season ends. Ash left in an unused stove soaks up moisture like blotting paper, and the rust that follows can put pressure on the stove's joints and damage them. Leave the air control handle slightly open so air moves through. Keep rainwater out of the flue with a chimney cap, but don't block the flue completely. A desiccant such as kitty litter in the stove bottom helps absorb summer moisture; remove it before the heating season.

chimney.title: Chimney, creosote & yearly checks
chimney.html:
Burning wood slowly makes tar and vapors that condense in a cool chimney as creosote. If creosote ignites, it makes an extremely hot fire.

How often to check

  • To start with, check for soot above the baffle plate and around the flue outlet about once a month.
  • Inspect the chimney connector and chimney at least once every two months in the heating season, and remove any creosote buildup.
  • If the stove suddenly turns sluggish, check for fallen soot around the flue collar or in the chimney.
  • Clean the flue after every heating season, and inspect it before the next one for bird's nests or other blockages.

To look yourself, let the stove cool completely, then use a mirror to sight up through the flue collar. If you can't inspect or clean it yourself, call a professional chimney sweep or your Morsø dealer.

Before each heating season

Thoroughly clean the chimney and connector and check them for damage. Check the gaskets for wear, the glass for cracks, and the door and handles for tightness.

Chimney fire? Act promptly: close the air control, get everyone out of the house, and call the fire department.

safety.title: Safe burning & over-firing
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; contact can burn skin.
  • Keep furniture at least 42 inches from the stove, and keep drying clothes, newspapers, firewood and other movable combustibles 42 inches away too.
  • Run it with the door fully closed. Never leave it unattended with the door open: gas and flame can be drawn out of the opening.
  • Fit a smoke detector in the room where the stove is installed.
  • Never burn overnight.
  • Burn wood only. Other fuels can release toxic fumes.
  • Wear safety goggles and gloves for maintenance.

Signs of over-firing

Do not over-fire the stove. If any part of the stove or the chimney connector glows, you are over-firing. Over-firing can cause a house fire or permanently damage the stove.

Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen up a fire, and keep them away from the stove while it's in use.

blower.title: The blower
blower.html:
The blower kit is thermostat-controlled. Its heat-activated sensor is held by a magnet to the heat shield under the firebox, and it lets the blower operate when the stove reaches the required running temperature.

BlowerIn the blower housing, behind the front access door under the firebox
Speed controllerAcross the ventilation grill at the front right of the blower housing base
Power cordLeaves through a cut-out in the left or right side of the convection box

The kit includes the blower unit, the speed controller, the magnetic thermostat sensor and cable ties for the cord. It can be fitted without removing the insert. The replacement blower, including speed control, is a Fasco B22508 (Morsø part 54560100).

Magnets hold the blower to the base and back wall of its chamber, and the fan's mouth must face upward.

warranty.title: Guarantee & wear parts
warranty.html:
If your stove was supplied by an authorised Morsø dealer, Morsø gives a 10-Year Manufacturers Guarantee against manufacturing defects in the main exterior body parts. You can register the stove online; the guarantee page gives the web address.

Not covered by the guarantee

  • The flame-path parts: firebricks, glass, baffle, pilot air assembly and flue collar
  • The ceramic rope
  • The paint finish

Flame-path parts take the full heat of the fire and need replacing from time to time as routine maintenance. Buy them from your Morsø dealer, don't use substitutes, and replace damaged parts as soon as possible. Persistent heavy firing, and soot and ash left to build up, wear them out faster.

Door gasket

The rope gasket around the door can harden over time. Replace it if the door gets hard to close, or if air leaks in around the door and the fire becomes less controllable. A Morsø rope gasket kit is available from your stove supplier.

If over-firing distorts the baffle, the stove still works but may be less efficient. Replace the baffle as soon as possible.

specFireplace.title: Minimum masonry fireplace
specFireplace.html:
Height (A)26" / 660 mm
Depth (B)19¼" / 490 mm
Width (C)28¾" / 730 mm

Approved in the US and Canada for a masonry fireplace or the Morsø Fireplace Insert Zero Clearance Enclosure (separate instructions). Do not install in a factory-built fireplace or in a transportable building / mobile home. The letters refer to a drawing in the manual.

Maker's website: Mobile Home Approved (US only) Yes. Install to the manual.
  • Chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner.

specFlue.title: Chimney & connector
specFlue.html:
Chimney linerContinuous, 6" diameter, insert to top of chimney
Liner system listingUL 1777 (USA) · ULC S635 (Canada)
Liner classClass 3, CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640
Connector6 inches (150mm)
Stainless steel connectorAt least 8 feet long
ChimneyMasonry, or listed type HT factory-built: UL-103-1985 (2100º F.) / ULC S-629 (650ºC)
Chimney heightAt least 16 feet recommended (not required), flue collar to top
Maker's website: Flue Outlet Top 150, Flue Outlet Rear 150. Install to the manual.
  • Connector and chimney not less than 6" internal (or equivalent cross section) and not significantly larger, or flue gases cool and performance turns sluggish or unpredictable.
  • One flueway per appliance: never a flue serving another appliance, never an air distribution duct.
  • Seal every joint airtight from heater to chimney outlet; support the flue system independently of the stove.
  • Connector: 24 MSG black or blue, or listed double-wall; single-wall 24 gauge or heavier; no galvanized. Minimum three screws to the product and to each adjoining section.
  • Mild bends (45º rather than 90º); keep all venting accessible for cleaning; not through an attic, closet or similar concealed space.
Note: p. 9 says the insert must be installed with a continuous 6" chimney liner from the insert to the top of the chimney; p. 5 says the chimney must have a clay liner or a stainless steel liner, with a stainless steel connector at least 8 feet long; and p. 7 says to connect the flue collar to "the flue pipe (or 8 feet stainless steel connector) or the flexible chimney liner".
Note: p. 9 recommends a chimney height of at least 16 feet above the stove (not required); the sample-installation drawing on p. 11 labels the liner Minimum 16" high.

specAir.title: Fresh air inlet
specAir.html:
Dedicated fresh air inlet2 square inches (1250 square mm) of free air space

Particularly important where the room is well sealed, or where an extractor hood or ventilation system disturbs the natural air pressure.

  • Air flow within the insert may not be altered.

specBlower.title: Blower kit
specBlower.html:
Blower incl. speed controlFasco B22508 · SKU 54560100
Mounting plate, speed controlSKU 71563100

Kit: thermostat-controlled blower unit, speed controller, cable ties, magnetic thermostat sensor. Fits without removing the insert.

  • Blower sits on the base of the convection chamber, to the rear, centered between the two rectangular ventilation holes, in the blower housing behind the front access door. Magnets hold it to the base and back wall; the fan mouth must face upward.
  • Thermostat sensor attaches magnetically to the heat shield at the roof of the blower housing (underside of the firebox) and allows the blower to operate when the stove reaches running temperature.
  • Power cord exits left or right through the cut-outs in the convection box side walls; secure it with the cable ties, using the securing points at the front left and right of the blower housing door as the final fixed point.
  • Speed controller mounts across the ventilation grill at the front right of the blower housing base with the two hex-head bolts supplied.

review.notes: Single manual (installation & operation, 28 pages); no French or garbled text. The manual prints decimals with commas (71,4%; 1,5-2 lbs/piece; 1-1,5 inch ash layer); the guide writes them with points, so check_numbers.py reports '71.4' as not found although p. 3 prints '71,4%'. p. 12 has no extractable text (presumably a drawing; p. 10 refers to 'the clearance paragraph page 12' while the clearance table text is on p. 13). The lettered dimensions (fireplace A-C on p. 5, clearances A-E on p. 13) are defined on drawings; the guide uses only the text labels and values. p. 4 says the fireplace-size figure is for the 'Morsø 5660 Standard insert'; the guide uses p. 5's minimum masonry fireplace size. The fresh air inlet sentence on p. 14 reads inverted ('Unless there is deemed to be insufficient residual air ... a dedicated fresh air inlet will be needed'); flagged in the specAir drawer. The parts list calls the handle under the door 'Secondary draft control' / 'Handle sek. draught control' (p. 25), while the operating text (p. 17) calls the air controller beneath the door primary air; the guide follows the operating text. No troubleshooting chart or code table; fault panels are built from fault descriptions on pp. 9, 16, 17-22 and 28. Not covered by the manual, so left out: blower electrical rating, wiring or speed-control settings; burn times; firebox volume; overall insert dimensions; heating area; an outside-air kit (catalog says outside air 'available', the manual covers only a room fresh-air inlet). Catalog dimensions (23.07 x 27.95 x 17.17 in), firebox 1.15 cu ft and 2,200 sq ft heating area could not be checked. Guarantee page (p. 27) gives only the 10-year exterior body parts terms and a registration web address; exclusions are on p. 21. 'Never burn overnight' comes from the p. 28 quick guide.
